title: The Journey to the Great Oz

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: The Lion jumps over the ditch yesterday.
The Lion jumping over the ditch yesterday.
The Lion jumped over the ditch yesterday.
questions.rule: yesterday shows the past, so use the simple past: jumped.

options: Dorothy was tired, so she rode on the Lion's back.
Dorothy was tired, so she ride on the Lion's back.
Dorothy were tired, so she rode on the Lion's back.
questions.rule: so joins a cause and its result; both parts are in the past: was tired, rode.

options: The second gulf was more wider than the first.
The second gulf was widest than the first.
The second gulf was wider than the first.
questions.rule: Comparing two things: short adjective + -er than: wider than (never more wider).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Last week is the past. The past of fly is flew.

questions.rule: With than, use the -er form: much taller than.
and joins two similar ideas: big and strong.
The past of shake is shook (irregular verb); shaken needs has/had.
Subject + past verb + adverb: The Lion roared loudly.

options: I readed a story about Oz.
I reading a story about Oz.
I read a story about Oz.
questions.rule: The past of read is spelt read too (said 'red'); readed is not a word.

chat: Who is lighter, the Scarecrow or the Tin Woodman?
options: The Scarecrow is lighter than the Tin Woodman.
The Scarecrow is lightest than the Tin Woodman.
The Scarecrow is more light than the Tin Woodman.
questions.rule: Comparing two: lighter than.

options: The Woodman spoke softly to Dorothy.
The Woodman spoke soft to Dorothy.
The Woodman spoke softness to Dorothy.
questions.rule: To tell how he spoke, use the -ly adverb: softly.
fall is irregular: the past is fell.

options: Dorothy held Toto in her arms and climbed on the Lion's back.
Dorothy held Toto in her arms and climb on the Lion's back.
Dorothy holds Toto in her arms and climbed on the Lion's back.
questions.rule: Verbs joined by and keep the same tense: held ... and climbed.

Comparing two ditches with than: broader.

and joins two actions: Run and jump.

chat: How should we cross the road?
questions.rule: How asks about manner: use the -ly adverb carefully, and base verb after should.

options: The Kalidahs were more big than the Lion.
The Kalidahs were biggest than the Lion.
The Kalidahs were bigger than the Lion.
questions.rule: big becomes bigger (double g) when comparing two.

options: It was an eventful day for the travellers.
It was an eventfully day for the travellers.
It was a eventful day for the travellers.
questions.rule: Before a noun use the adjective eventful (-ful); it starts with a vowel sound, so an.

Comparing two: adjective + -er than: stronger than.
The adverb happily tells how she smiled (happy + -ly, y becomes i).

chat: How did the Lion cross the ditch?
options: He jump across it in one big leap.
He jumped across it in one big leaps.
He jumped across it in one big leap.
questions.rule: Past question, so jumped; one takes the singular leap.

options: Juice, please, because I am thirsty.
Juice, please, because I is thirsty.
questions.rule: After because we need a full sentence: I am thirsty.
After did, use the base form: What did he say?

options: Riya ran fastest than Aman because she practised every day.

Riya ran faster than Aman because she practise every day.

the ... in the world compares with all others: use -est: the highest.

Past question: Where did + subject + base verb (live)?
so comes before the result: the road was dark, so Toto stayed close.

options: It was great! I run faster than last time.
It was great! I ran fastest than last time.
It was great! I ran faster than last time.
questions.rule: The race is over: ran (past); with than, use faster.

chat: How was your day at the science fair?
options: It was very eventful and exciting!
It was very eventfully and exciting!
It was very eventful and excite!
questions.rule: After was, use adjectives: eventful and exciting.

The Lion could not jumped the second gulf because it was too broad.
The Lion could not jump the second gulf because it were too broad.

chat: Did you finish the Oz book?
options: Not yet. I started it, but I did not finished it.
Not yet. I start it, but I did not finish it.
Not yet. I started it, but I did not finish it.
questions.rule: but joins the opposite ideas; after did not, use the base form finish.

chat: Which was the most exciting part of the story?
options: The fight with the Kalidahs was the most exciting part.
The fight with the Kalidahs were the most exciting part.
The fight with the Kalidahs was the most excitingest part.
questions.rule: The subject is the fight (singular): was; long adjectives take the most, not -est.
